a.text: I don't like the throne room in the Palace of Westhaleg. It's so empty and bleak.
That lonely throne just sitting there—I can't imagine what it'd be like if Vina actually sat on it.
One woman, on that cold, lifeless chair, staring at the barren steps...
Knowing Vina, she wouldn't last a minute there—I'd bet on it.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Did you find the crown? Where is it?

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: We didn't find it, per se. Someone delivered it to the Speaker's office. We can't determine the precise time it was lost, but we're fairly certain it happened after your speech started.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Vina already placed the crown on that empty throne... so what's the point of stealing it? Was it an order from the dukes?

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: I don't think so.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: The dukes are never of one mind—they each have their own agenda. However, for the crown to go missing at the same time they're visiting Londinium? That's far too much of a coincidence.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: But, according to what you've told us, isn't that crown just an old, rusted hunk of iron now?

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: ....Umm, not exactly, Morgan.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: To many people, the crown is extraordinarily important, no matter its current state.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: It's been left untouched for over twenty years, but the people have not forgotten about it. In fact, they are more eager than ever for its return.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: They're waiting for a wise new monarch to put it on his/her head, someone who can dispel the shadows hanging over Victoria.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: No, most people are just desperate for a miracle—something that can satisfy their craving for royal authority.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: I cannot deny that. Plus, you have listened to their voices for ages, Vina.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Your identity is truly unique: a descendant of the royal family and a bona fide war hero who was nonetheless raised on the streets. It's no wonder so many people naturally feel drawn to you.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Now that Parliament is up and running and the dukes have willingly relinquished their authority, the people are all the more convinced that you've secured universal support.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: The next step is plain as day.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: But the dukes have no intentions of doing anything like that!

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: The public only cares about the outcome, Morgan.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Yes… I've understood that since the day we returned home. Unfortunately, sometimes, I'm still very good at letting people down.

steps.name: Carefree Citizen
steps.text: Thank you for sharing the energy bars, Eliseo. I'll gladly undergo daily sampling, if I get tasty treats like this every time. Haha.

steps.name: Carefree Citizen
steps.text: Are these really things you can just buy off the shelf in Columbia? Why do you Columbians stock up on stuff like this—is it for Catastrophe or something?

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: These bars are my own personal thing.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: 'Food is fuel.' It's about energy and nutrition. Energy bars are convenient, so why not?

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: Then again, Diane definitely disagrees with me on this. She's more of a foodie.

steps.name: Carefree Citizen
steps.text: I understand. We're thankful just to fill our bellies in Londinium these days.

steps.name: Carefree Citizen
steps.text: Her Royal Highness Alexandrina has worked very hard to ensure that we have enough food to eat.

steps.name: Impatient Citizen
steps.text: Quit yapping his ear off, will you?

steps.name: Impatient Citizen
steps.text: Thank you, Eliseo, for these...uh...'energy bars,' but we'd best be on our way now.

steps.name: Carefree Citizen
steps.text: Stanley, you're not afraid that Eliseo will...?

steps.name: Impatient Citizen
steps.text: Of course not!

steps.name: Impatient Citizen
steps.text: I... surely I can't be arguing with you about such stupid things in front of someone else, right? It's not proper.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Carefree Citizen
steps.text: *sigh* He doesn't like when I refer to Alexandrina as 'Her Royal Highness', That's all.

steps.name: Carefree Citizen
steps.text: He and I don't see eye to eye politically. I think having a king again wouldn't be half bad, but he insists life was worse for us when the monarchy was still in power.

steps.name: Carefree Citizen
steps.text: But think about it, whether it was back then, or right now, aren't we managing to get by all the same?

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: So you're saying the presence of a monarch doesn't really impact your life all that much?

steps.name: Impatient Citizen
steps.text: It doesn't matter what she thinks. Even if someone does ascend the throne again, it's not like we'll be invited to the coronation feast.

steps.name: Carefree Citizen
steps.text: *sigh* Stanley, when are you going to come up with an argument that actually convinces me?

steps.name: Carefree Citizen
steps.text: Sorry about this, Eliseo. I need to talk some sense into this stubborn mule.

steps.name: Carefree Citizen
steps.text: Oh, by the way, about the increased patrols in the city—I've heard a rumor. Supposedly, someone stole the crown, and the Defense Forces are investigating anyone who might be connected with the theft.

steps.name: Carefree Citizen
steps.text: Let's go, Stanley. Goodbye, Eliseo.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: Come to think of it, Diane has never mentioned the king or the crown, not even once. Maybe I should ask her about it when I get back.

steps.name: Sanatorium Patient
steps.text: Eliseo, you should take a break. You've been working nearly nonstop, helping collect patient data.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: The city's Infected all experienced acute infection around the same time, with many showing rare pathological progressions. I need to document this valuable data thoroughly.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: Whether it's for future research into Oripathy or for developing targeted treatments for Londinium's citizens, this data is critically important.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: By the way, Sarah, why didn't Diane visit you today?

steps.name: Sanatorium Patient
steps.text: Diane?

steps.name: Sanatorium Patient
steps.text: I thought she was helping you. Many of my old comrades came by the sanatorium today. They wanted to ask if anything 'unusual' had come up recently. We were hoping to bring Diane along for a little reunion with them.

a.text: Throughout the whole war, Vina never told us where she found that crown.
But it didn't matter. None of us cared, and no one would ever see that hunk of iron again.
It was supposed to remain sealed in the throne room in the Palace of Westhaleg, left to corrode and decay into nothing.
'The Age of Kings is over and done.'
That's what a drunken Vina said to me, with her arm slung around my neck.
And yet, barely two months later, here it is again, staring us in the face—The ghost of this ancient empire refuses to let go. It's always ready to claim its next victim.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Does anyone else know about this?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: We've taken steps to contain the information and will do everything we can to minimize its impact.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: So... what do we do with this thing?
Morgan points at the battered crown sitting on the desk.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: This is my first time seeing it up close. Can't believe so many people are fretting over this old thing...

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Vina... Vina?
She notices that Vina isn't looking at the crown at all. Instead, she's standing silently by the desk, her gaze fixed on the dejected figure sitting in the chair across from her—
'The one who stole the crown'.

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: You really have no questions for me, Madam Speaker?

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: I reckon many of you have fanciful notions about me.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Besides, my colleagues will soon have a more complete and objective report delivered to my desk, regarding this matter. So—

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: Don't lump me in with those people! All they care about is the throne itself. I care about the one on the throne.

spans.text: Don't lump me in with those people! All they care about is the throne itself. I care about the one

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: I know exactly what I'm doing. I'm well aware of every new law Parliament has enacted, Speaker Vina. Unauthorized entry into the throne chamber is indeed a serious crime, and I'm not planning to deny anything.
Vina shakes her head.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: But that doesn't mean you're fundamentally different from those people. The provisional court will try your case according to the law.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Do you have any further objections?

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: No, Madam Speaker.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Delphine, I'll leave the rest to you. I'll personally return the crown to the throne room and make sure security is tightened up.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: *sigh* And then I need to prepare the report for the council meeting—

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: Heh... a report.

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: You didn't have to do all this, Siege. You know all too well how inefficient Parliament is—it's just a group of individuals all looking out for their own self-interest.

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: You must already be exhausted, just from dealing with all those MPs, no?

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: Londinium has no need for a Speaker operating at the whims of Parliament. What Londinium needs is a real, absolute leader who can guide the city through its transformation.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Vina, there's no point in arguing with her about this meaningless stuff.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: I know, Delphine. Madam, are you suggesting that Londinium needs a dictator?

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: No. I'm talking about a king. Victoria needs a king.

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: I can guess what you want to do, Madam Speaker. You're unlike any ruler I've ever known.

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: You don't even care about your own lineage. But if you wish to achieve your vision, 'Speaker', it won't be enough. This crown should not, and will not, become an obstacle to you.
She stands up, giving Vina a crisp salute.

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: That is all I have to say on this matter.

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: I give my thanks to The Exemplars, and The Siege, for all you've done for our homeland.

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: I'm fond of the changes she's undergone and firmly believe she'll become an even better leader in future.

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: It's just a shame that her transformation is still so slow... I won't live to see that day myself.

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: Let's go, Lady Delphine. Where should we head next?

a.text: 'Do you really know what I wish to do?'
'You want to change Victoria...'
'No. You want to defeat her. You want to defeat the Victoria of the past.'

steps.text: Vina stands at the foot of the staircase, holding the crown in her hands as she gazes at the throne.
Beside the throne, a golden lion lays sprawled, his eyelids drooping halfway.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Gawain, you should've told me sooner.
Step by step, she ascends the staircase until she reaches the throne. Instead of sitting on it, she sits on the steps before it.
The lion doesn't seem to open his eyes. His gentle breath brushes through its mane, sending up faint specks of dust.
He is displeased.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: I'm sorry, Gawain. I had another sleepless night. There are still so many thorny issues left unresolved...
She feels the warmth at her back. The golden lion has moved closer, and his massive body is now supporting her.
Just like it had when she was a child. Vina catches a whiff of sunlight.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Gawain, how nice it would be to fall asleep leaning against you like this.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Walking all the way back here from outside the city feels like... a dream...

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: But it's been so long since I've had a good night's sleep, let alone a deep, satisfying dream.
The lion lifts his head slightly, brushing against Vina's golden hair, tickling her just enough to make her smile faintly.
The chill in the air sends a shiver through her, jolting her back to clarity.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: ...Has it always been this cold here? It's not time to rest yet, is it?

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: What we're doing now still falls far short. There's not enough medicine, not enough food, and endless arguments—

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Sometimes I wish I could just rip off this uniform and knock those idiots down one by one. Maybe things would be much simpler that way, huh?

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: 'Defeat the Victoria of the past'...

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: If only it were as simple as a match in the ring.
The golden lion closes his eyes, drifting off to sleep, though his tail is still lazily swatting against Vina's arm.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Teacher, I'm sorry for complaining to you again.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: There are some things I don't know how to explain to Morgan and the others. They wouldn't understand, and I don't want to make them worry.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: As for Delphine... I don't want to show too much doubt or vulnerability in front of her. She's already taken on so much for me and pinned so many expectations on me.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: There are already so many people counting on me, Gawain.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: I don't want to let them down.
She shuts her eyes and grips the crown.
'King', 'Speaker', these titles mean nothing to her.
She just wants—

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Vina, I knew I'd find you here!

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Wait… were you just asleep, or?

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: No, I was just thinking about something. Gawain, he—
She instinctively turns her head to the side, but there's no one there. Yet that warmth remains, unmistakable.
He's gone.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: (...Thank you for being here with me, Gawain.)

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Morgan, what are you doing here?

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Delphine convinced the provisional court to hold the crown thief in the Defense Forces' detention quarters, for now.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: The full report on her is out now. I didn't want to waste time, so I came straight to you. Here, this is the report.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Her name is Diane Weber.
Morgan pauses, watching Vina closely for a reaction. But Vina simply looks at her with curiosity, waiting for her to continue.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: She didn't just decide to steal the crown out of the blue.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: She has been working with a pharmaceutical rep from Columbia for a while now, helping spread awareness about Oripathy infection protection methods.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: That's how she learned when the guards patrolling outside the Palace of Westhaleg would change shifts. Once she got inside, she waited until your speech and slipped into the throne room.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: And then, she stayed there for quite a while—at least half an hour.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: What did she do in there?

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: I don't know, and she won't say. Maybe she was hesitating, or maybe she just got lost in thought. In any case, she managed to make off with the crown without alerting anyone.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Wait, something doesn't add up here. She stayed in the throne chamber for so long. She didn't run into the patrols after the shift change?

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: No, she didn't. Even she was surprised by how easily she escaped. She thought for sure the patrols would catch her.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: So someone must have helped her. Was it one of the guests?

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Unclear, but if she had help, she didn't know about it. She came up with this whole plan herself.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: But... why? Just to bring the crown to me and goad me into—

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Her name is Diane Weber.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: I know—

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: You don't remember her. I kept thinking she looked familiar, and when I saw the report, I realized—it's her.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Remember that day when the alliance surrounded us on our doorstep? The first soldier to defy orders and escort us forward?
Vina recalled the sky that day, filled with steam, the lingering smell of smoke and gunpowder.
And the soldier whose face had become a blur in her memory.

a.text: 'This is Lieutenant Diane Weber of the Sixth Column, Tenth Infantry Regiment. Lower your weapons, soldiers, and escort the Exemplars in their advance.'
'Before I was a soldier, I was a Londinier. This is my home too.'
'Go, Siege. The fight is not yet over.'
'We will take back what is ours!'

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Diane Weber, the soldier who defied the Duke of Caster's orders... She contracted an acute infection in the final battle against the Nachzehrer King.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: That rings a bell? She was the one who took the Sighs of Kings from you and charged towards the Nachzehrers.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: She doesn't have much time left.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: We are short of Oripathy suppressants, and she never got enough medicine to slow her condition. We took a look at her, but—
The crown lets out a faint metallic creak as Vina's hand tightens around it. It looks so fragile, yet its resilience is undeniable.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: She really loved our home, and she loved Victoria as well.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: That's why she volunteered to join the ducal forces, only to defy their orders and end up forced into retirement.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: She trusted you, even though I don't agree with some of her ideas. Vina, maybe we could...

a.text: I never finished asking for mercy on Diane's behalf. Vina knew what I wanted to say, and I knew how she'd respond...
No, I knew what Speaker Vina Victoria would say.
Even now, I can't imagine what must've been going through Diane Weber's head when she made that crazy decision, but I admire her.
...Even though she stole the crown, she did it out of love for Victoria.
I don't understand. Since coming back to the city, so many things have changed—changed in ways I can't fathom and don't want to understand.
And on that day, I finally made up my mind—
From the end of that final battle outside the Palace of Westhaleg until now... I've lingered here far too long.
Maybe it's time to go home, back to the boxing gym.
